utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. As you know, today we have -- we have a witness who is testifying via videolink. I understand that the technology is all set up and we're ready to go.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: --- Break taken at 8.12 a.m.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I may respond with regard to the quoted pages. Given that we dealt with the statement of this witness, we don't have to deal with this, however we need to address the issue of the witness's testimony in the Popovic case. So apart from that, we do not wish to tender anything else into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: Any observations, Ms. West?

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: I don't. I'm not -- I'm not clear what Mr. Karadzic means as to we need to address the witness's evidence in the Popovic case. That was admitted as an exhibit, so I don't -- I don't have any comment otherwise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: So, we'll leave it at that.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe I wasn't quite clear. I said that part of the questions pertained to the transcript that was already in evidence, whereas the other questions pertained to the statements given by the witness. The witness confirmed them. And for that reason we are tendering them into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: Well, I assume that that was the position, Dr. Karadzic, but thank you for making it plain.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Your Honour, we would call Investigator Tomasz Blaszczyk, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, while we are waiting for the witness, with your leave I will just correct: The document 30867, instead of C3, would we have C4, since C3 was already taken. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: Good morning. Let the witness take the solemn declaration, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: Thank you. If you'd like to sit and make yourself comfortable. And having taken the declaration in English, are you content to use English as the language of response, or it doesn't matter if you don't, whichever you prefer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: English is okay, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, Ms. West.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: What is your name?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: My name is Tomasz Blaszczyk.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Sir, and you testified twice before in this case most recently in January of this year but, prior to that, in August of 2010; is that right?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: Yes. This is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Can you tell us what the general subject matter of the testimony that you gave in August 2010, please?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: In August 2010, I testified in this trial about the notebooks seized at the house of General Ratko Mladic on -- in December 2008 and in February 2010.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: And besides the notebooks that were seized during those two searches, were other items seized as well?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: Yes. Except, apart that notebooks were seized in -- during these two searches, also there were other items like -- especially the second search in February 2010, there was seized also medical documentation of General Ratko Mladic, some documents, some audiotapes, video-tapes, DVDs, CDs, and dictaphone tapes.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Okay. And that's what we're going to focus on today. We're not going to focus on the first search, from December of 2008, we're going to focus on the second search, which is February 2010. When did you first receive information that the search had taken place?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: The OTP received this information that the search occurred shortly after it happened, after in -- I believe it was end of February 2010.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: And in March did you receive some information about what was seized?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: Yes. In -- on the 29 of March, OTP received a hard drive containing the scanned version of the documents seized at General Ratko Mladic place and also the copy of -- of the tapes, audiotapes, video-tapes, CDs seized in the same location on 23 of February, 2010.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: And subsequent to that was the original material, the actual items that were seized, were they delivered to the ICTY?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: Yes. At the request of OTP, the Serbian authorities delivered these -- the seized material to our field office in Belgrade. It happened on 27 April 2010.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Did you have an opportunity to go there and see it yourself?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: Yes, I did. In May, beginning of May and 7 of May I went to Belgrade field office, and on 9 of May I reviewed this material personally. I mean, I checked the receipt or the list of the material physically with the material itself at our field office if Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: So let's back up. Between the time of April 27 and May 9th, where was this material held?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: The material was held at our field office in Belgrade at investigate -- at investigator's room, our investigator from the field office, and material was secured and locked entire time between 27 and 9 of -- in fact 10 of May, 2010.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: And when you arrived there in May, what did you do regarding that material?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: As I said already, we -- we checked the inventory list and physically the material locked at this investigation room in Belgrade field office, and we packed -- I packed this material to diplomatic bag and I drove this material, I think I drove the car, but together with material we drove together with my colleague investigator to -- to The Hague. And we arrived at the The Hague on the 11 of May -- May, 2010, and the same day delivered this material to our Evidence Unit.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: And once you set eyes on the material when you arrived in Belgrade to the moment that it arrived at the evidence unit here in The Hague, was the material always within your custody?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: Yes, it's correct. In fact, you know, when we checked the material on the 9th of May, 2010, we -- we sealed this material in this diplomatic bag and we left the bag at our field office also in secure room, room in Belgrade, and the following day on the 10th, the morning, we -- we drove to -- to The Hague.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: And since -- since then, the material was entire time with me until I delivered this material to our Evidence Unit here in The Hague.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: May we have 65 ter 22939.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: I'd like to talk about the items that were seized. Excluding the notebooks. We're not going to talk about the notebooks. So we're going to look at 65 ter 22939. This is a report dated April 30th, 2010. Do you see that in front of you now?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Okay. Is this something you recognise?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: Yes, I do. I recognise this -- this document. We received this document from -- from Republic of Serbia. This is -- this is a report of the contents of the seized documentation from -- from Ratko Mladic house.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Okay. And I think we all see it now. Yes.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Okay. You said this is a report of the contents of the seized documentation. Can you tell us - I'm just understanding it's a report - is there some analysis involved with it as well?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: Yes. I said content, but this is a kind of analysis, what is -- what was exactly seized - what was in the notebooks, what was in the documentation, what was on the tapes.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: All right. And this is a very lengthy report, but does this report include all the items that were seized and brought back to The Hague?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct. All the items which were handed over to OTP are included in this report.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: And how do you know that this report and list is consistent with what was actually seized?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: I read this report. I checked this report. I compared this report also with -- with other documents we've received from the search and with all we received.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Okay. If we can have e-court page 348 of this, please. Does this listing also include a number of recordings or tapes?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: Yes. This is correct. The list includes also quite big number of -- of the tapes.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: And can you estimate how many tapes it includes?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: If I could remember, there were about 100 tapes, audiotapes, dictaphone tapes, and other tapes. Also CDs, some CDs, and DVDs.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: All right. So we're looking at page 338 and I want to focus on one example of this. We can see number 33, it says: "One dictation tape without header." Can you tell us what it means by "dictation tape"?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is small tape used for dictaphones in sometime ago when you are using dictaphones to record some conversation or whatever. And we use also the small teeny tapes, and this is this type of tape. If I could remember from the picture I seen, this is tape -- Olympus tape, small dictaphone Olympus tape.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: All right. And specifically in regard to what's listed at number 33, have you yourself reviewed this tape?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: Yes, I reviewed this tape. I reviewed the tape and also I reviewed the transcript done later on from this tape.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: If we were to go through the rest of this report, several times we see that it reflects dictaphone tapes. Do you know why there are recordings on dictaphone tapes, if you know?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: I have some assumption why it was recorded on these dictaphone tapes, but -- but why exactly we never -- we never got answer for this question.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Okay. Then I'll leave it there.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: May we have P04484, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: So this is a transcript of a conversation.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Thank you. That's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: This is a transcript of a conversation, what looks to be between Zivanovic and Mr. Karadzic. Now, I'm not going to review this particular -- the substance of this particular recording -- recording with you, because this was already discussed with Witness Obradovic on February 27th of this year, but specifically as to this recording, can you tell us how this recording came into OTP possession?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: This is a recording on the tape or this dictaphone tape seized also at the house of General Ratko Mladic on 23 February 2010 and later on handed over to OTP.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: And is this one of the recordings that you yourself transported from Belgrade back to The Hague?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: Yes. This is -- this is correct. This is part of the material I transported to The Hague on 11 May 2010.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: And does this recording correspond to what we just looked at at page 380 -- excuse me, 348 in the big listing? Is this the recording that's listed there or one of the recordings that's listed there?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: Yes. This is correct. This is -- they are talking about the same recording.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: And how do you know that?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: If you look at the contents of this recording from our transcript and if we look at the describe of -- done in this report, Serbian MUP report, we see that this is the same tape. And also, as I told Your Honour at the beginning, first we received the hard drive containing the scanned version of the material seized in Ratko Mladic house, and also the audio recordings on these -- on this hard drive. And I compared the number - even the number -- this number 33 - 33 is the number of the items marked by the Serbian MUP during the search. This is the same item.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Now, you -- you mentioned the way we acquired this particular recording was you yourself drove it back. Are all the other recordings listed in the big sheet acquired by the OTP in the same way?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would tender 65 ter 22939, which is the inventory sheet.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, we would object to the entire document being admitted. If there's any portion such as the page that she's referred to that show the origin of a particular item that's being admitted into evidence, we don't object to that portion, but we don't believe that the entire 440-page document should be admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: Ms. West.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would say that this witness has already indicated that he looked at this entire document. He himself viewed the actual items seized. He compared two. And he's the custodian that brought this material back to The Hague. I would submit that this is just a documentation reflecting what he in fact did and it should be admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. President, it's not relevant to anything except for the pages that have been referenced, and it describes a lot of documents and other things that have been seized, summarises conversations that have not been introduced into evidence, and so we think that there's a lot of irrelevant material in that document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: As much in the interests of volume economy of material, the Chamber is minded to agree with the intervention by Mr. Robinson as to this. So just those -- those portions which are actually referred to in evidence at this stage in the trial will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. So if I'm to understand, that should be the first page and page 348, which is the page that we spoke about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The pages of document 22939 will receive number P4908, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would also like to speak to P4484, which is the transcript of the recording that the witness has just spoken about, and I would ask that this be admitted for all purposes. And if I may give a little bit of background on this. This was a recording that was discussed with Witness Obradovic on February 27th of this year, and he was asked several questions about the substance and the content of the recording itself. This is a recording this is not actually an intercept. It's, as you heard, on a dictaphone. So it's a recording of a conversation, but it's not an intercept. At that point, the Prosecution had asked that it be exceptionally accepted into evidence. The witness at the time had recognised Mr. Karadzic's voice and spoke about the content of the conversation. There had been an objection at the time for lack of foundation and the President also agreed and he indicated that there would be a needed foundation, perhaps placed by this witness, Mr. Blaszczyk, as to how the recording came into our possession. I would submit that the OTP has now done that and I would ask that it be admitted substantively.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: No objection, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: So be it. It will be admitted as requested, for all purposes.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Thank you. If we can have P04359, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Sir, this is an interview - at the top it says July 13th, 1995 - with Radovan Karadzic, and this is an interview that the Trial Chamber has seen before, specifically on February 8th, with Mr. Karadzic's secretary who was a witness, Ms. Mihajlovic. Sir, are you familiar with this interview?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: Yes, I am familiar with this interview.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: And what were the circumstances under which you became aware of it?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: First, I remember it was, I believe, 2005 or 2006, we -- we had in possession already the interview in newspaper "El Pais" with Radovan Karadzic. The Spanish journalist conducted this interview with Radovan Karadzic. And later on in 2008 we requested from the Spain authorities to have a copy of actual recording of this interview, and we received this copy of these recordings. I believe it was 2008, October.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: And have you yourself listened to the recording?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Did you recognise one of the voices?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: Yes, I did recognise the voice of Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Did you compare the audio recording to the transcript?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: Yes, I did. I compared the audio recording with the transcript and the transcript is correct. The interview --

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Okay --

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: Sorry. The interview was conducted in English. It was quite easy for me to compare this transcript and recording itself.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: And was the subject matter upon which Mr. Karadzic spoke in the interview familiar to you?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: Yes, it is. Mr. Karadzic is speaking this interview about general situation in Bosnia, about political situation in Bosnia, about Serbs' position in this war in Bosnia, especially related to 1995, July 1995. And also there is some information about Srebrenica enclave.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: And did the subject matter relate to events that were unfolding at the time, on July 13th, 1995?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: Yes. The subject matter related to events which were followed after July 1995.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would again admit this exhibit for all purposes. And if I can give a little background on this. As I mentioned, this was a interview that was discussed with Witness Mihajlovic on February 8th, and she spoke about it in regard to the diary. She spoke about the interview actually taking place and it corresponded with the diary. At the time it was admitted for corroborating purposes only. There had been an object -- objection for lack of foundation. I would submit that that foundation has now been laid and I'd ask that it be admitted for all purposes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: No objection, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: Thank you. It will be so admitted. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Now, lastly, sir, if we can look at 65 ter 03935A. And for everyone in the courtroom: This is the handout that you have received. During your last testimony, this year, January of this year, you discussed the film footage that was made by Zoran Petrovic of some of the events related to Srebrenica. Do you remember that.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: Yes, I do remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: And can you just briefly remind the Trial Chamber what that footage entailed.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: Zoran Petrovic, this is Serbian journalist, he was in the area of Srebrenica and Bratunac on the 13 and 14 July 1995. In his footage he recorded some events in Potocari and some events along the road from Kravica towards Konjevic Polje, Kravica-Sandici-Pervani road.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: And in regard to his footage, were some still photographs produce of it?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: Yes, there were some photographs.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: And some of those stills that were produced, did you use that to produce your Petrovic road book?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: Yes. In this, my Petrovic road book, I compared the stills and the photographs from the Petrovic video with actual present or 2006 photographs of the same area.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Now, was another book also produced based in part of some of the stills from the Petrovic footage?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: Yes. The stills from the Petrovic footage was -- were used also for another book. We call it Bosnian Muslim photo identification book.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: And tell us what that book is all about.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: During our investigation related to the fall of Srebrenica, we tried to identify some person depicted on this footage, especially the Muslim -- also the Muslim -- Muslim men, and we -- we captured some stills from the Petrovic video. We -- we conducted investigation or we conducted some action that led us to identify the people from -- from this Petrovic video.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: How was the book organised?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: The book itself, I mean, this Bosnian Muslim photo identification book, has two parts. One parts contains the identification -- the pictures of the people identified by -- by us and who are -- at that time were on the missing list, ICMP missing list, and altogether we were able to identify 31 people, but only twenty -- not only, but only 7 of them were survivors, and 24 at that time were at the ICMP list.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: All right. I'm not going to show you the whole book because it's a little bit lengthy, but what you have in front of you, and I think you have a hard copy too, this is just four pages from the book, and if we can go to e-court page -- what would be 2, but first page of the book.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I have -- in front of me I have a binder containing these five pages, but also in the binder I have some corroborating material, if I can use this.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: So -- and we'll talk about that in a second if you have to use it.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: But if you can open up the book. And the page we have now, we see a line of males walking. And on -- and then we have three numbers - 1, 2, and 3. Can you tell us what that indicates?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: Indicates the people identified by our witnesses. And number 1, you know, just we see the man with -- we named him. We identified him through our witnesses. His name is Mehmedovic. Number 2, we see the man behind also with this red arrow. We -- in fact, in this footage, this still, we see only his -- his head, and his name is Ahmo Mehmedovic. And the third man, his name is Sevko Mujic, also identified by our witnesses. But this is only the footage. But if you -- we look at the Petrovic video, we can see that this column of the men are moving towards this road, and this is recordings from Potocari within -- I think this is between -- around the location of the white house in Potocari.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: And the information below each name, is that referring to the interview that was conducted that led to the identification?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct. Information below each name is -- this is the name of the person who identified this particular man on the picture, and we are referring to the OTP interview conducted at that time.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: We can --

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. President. I'm objecting to the introduction of statements by persons who the OTP have interviewed, including statements of identification, and I cite to the Trial Chamber the Appeals Chamber's decision on the admissibility of Prosecution investigator's evidence in the Slobodan Milosevic case on the 20th of September, 2002. There -- we've referred to this decision several times before this Trial Chamber, but essentially a Prosecution investigator by the name of Barney Kelly purported to summarise information given to him by OTP witnesses, and the Appeals -- the Trial Chamber and the Appeals Chamber held that that was not permissible, that, in fact, circumvented the requirements of Rule 92 bis which would have required that these witnesses at a minimum statements be admitted be and certified before they could be admitted, as opposed to being -- the information being conveyed to the Chamber by an investigator. And I think that this is a similar situation and therefore I would ask that any evidence of the identifications made by persons should be excluded. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Your Honour, perhaps I should have interrupted earlier, but these interviews are already admitted in the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: So each of the witnesses that he's talking about, they have been admitted under 92 bis?

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Okay. Then I withdraw my objection. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: So be it.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: If we can go to page 2, or the next page.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Here we see two individuals. Can you tell us about this still and where this was taken? Two individuals, excuse me, who are identified.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: Yeah. Through our witnesses we identified these two persons. The number 1, this is Kasim Hafizovic, and number 2 is Senahid Hafizovic. They were identified by the members of the family.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: And where was that still taken?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: This still is taken also in -- near the white house in Potocari on the 13 of July, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: May we go to the next page. This is ERN ending in 9765, page 3.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Where was this still taken?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: This -- this still is taken also on the same location in Potocari near the white house in Potocari on the 13 of July, 1995. And this still, we have three person identified by the members of their families. They are Bajram Malkic marked here as number 1; Betko Suljic, number 2; and Mevludin Pasagic, number 3.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: May we turn to the last page, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: What is the location of this still?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: This still has been captured in Sandici meadow on the 13 July 1995 afternoon-time, late afternoon-time.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: And was the individual we see here identified?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: Yes. This man is identified by his wife. His name is Ramo Osmanovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: May we briefly go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're back in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would tender 65 ter 03935A; it's a small booklet.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: So be it. That will be entered.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document will receive number P4909, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: Due to the rather odd timescale that's been adopted today, what we propose is to sit from now until 11.45 and then rise for 45 minutes until 12.30. So if you'd like to bear that in mind, Dr. Karadzic. Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I finish -- well, perhaps I may finish by the break. I would think that the Trial Chamber would not mind if that happened.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: I think you might be right about that, Dr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good day, Mr. Blaszczyk.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Have I pronounced your surname correctly?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: Yes. This is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. What I wanted to ask you is whether you were provided with some sort of an explanation or, rather, was this one of the searches of Mladic's house and not the first one by any means?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: No, it wasn't first search of this Mladic house. I'm referring to the search from 2010, February 2010. I know that -- that there were more searches, but at that time, as far as I know, the people from the Serbian MUP, they were more concentrate on -- on -- on Ratko Mladic as a person and just they were looking for him, but they didn't seize any material, according to my knowledge.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Were you then told that that material was in Mladic 's house all the time but they didn't examine it or take it or they didn't manage to find it at an earlier date?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: No, we didn't receive any confirmation that entire time. The material was in -- in this house, but -- but we got information from the Serbian authority that material was seized at this house on these particular dates.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Was there an explanation of any kind as to why the material was only seized in 2010 and not earlier on when numerous searches were conducted?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: As I said, you know, just explanation of the Serbian side was that they were more concentrate of the Ratko Mladic, to find him, than on the material from his house. Later on in 2008, they concentrated on the -- also on the material, wartime material. They seized this material. They handed over this material to us. At that time, as I testified already in August last year, they didn't find some notebooks of Ratko Mladic because according to them the notebooks were hidden somewhere in his house. As far as I remember, some of those notebooks were seized during the second search on the attic of bathroom of this apartment, this house.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know for certain that the Serbian authorities handed over everything that they seized?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: The Serbian authorities handed over the material we requested from them. At the beginning we received the information what was seized during these two searches, and based on that -- that -- this information and after reviewing the material, we requested these, the originals.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Does that mean that there was material that was found, material that you had not, in fact, searched for or requested?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: There -- there was also some material not relevant to any case to -- to ICTY job. For example, the material from the firm of son of Ratko Mladic, Darko Mladic, from 2000 years [sic], and not relevant to any ICTY cases. We didn't request to have the originals of this material at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could there have been something there that might have been of interest to the Defence?

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: Yes. That's so speculative, Dr. Karadzic, it's virtually incapable of being answered.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. In that case, I'll be more concrete.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Who decided about what was relevant, and who's position was, in fact, expressed in this manner? It was the Prosecution's position, was it not?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: I was involved in some extent in this project. I -- I -- in this -- I, personally, during the first search, I checked the material physically. I see this material before we requested the authority to hand it over, this material, to us. And yeah, there were investigators, mostly investigators who decided that the material is relevant to the ICTY cases. If we are talking about the originals. But, Your Honours, I would like to point out also that first we received the scanned version of the material, everything what was seized during these two searches. This scanned material of the materials, not originals, were also handed over to the Defence, if you are talking about whether any material was kept. It means that we may not have the original, some of the material, but definitely this -- the copy of this material, whatever document it was, is on the scanned version also handed over to the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. The material that you thought was irrelevant to the Tribunal, was that material also provided? Was it also provided to the Defence?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: I believe entire material, we receive first as a copy of the material, in fact, not originals, we handed over to the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you exclude the possibility that the Serbian authorities added certain material?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: The seizure of this material, it was the process -- process done by the Serbian MUP and then by Prosecution office in Serbia, and material seized by them from the Ratko Mladic house was confirm as seized from this house by the members of the family of Ratko Mladic, by his wife and by his son.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And how is it that you excluded the possibility that the material was amended in some way or that certain material was added?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: We have no such indication that this material was alterated [sic] in some way.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And that is the reason for which you didn't even attempt to check this; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: Your Honour, we reviewed this entire material. We reviewed each document from this -- this collection, I would say Mladic collection, and we didn't find any indication that this material was altered or false.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did the Serbian authorities carry out the analysis that you have mentioned, or was this someone else's responsibility? Did someone else do that?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: I mentioned our analyst. I am not referring to the Serbian analyst or information we -- for example, the document we seen before, a few minutes ago, on the screen, the Serbian report, but I am referring to our analyst.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now have a look at P4484 again.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: While waiting for it to come up: Mr. Blaszczyk, what explanation can be provided for my conversation with General Zivanovic, or, rather, a record of my conversation with General Zivanovic, being found in General Mladic's house?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: I believe I said that we have some assumption why -- why it happened and what happened exactly, according to our information, but it has not been so far proved, but we believe this is -- this is the reason that some conversations or telephone conversation -- conversation conducted from the Main Staff were recorded by the security branch of the Main Staff of Republika Srpska. And, of course, General Mladic as the commander of the Army of Republika Srpska has access to these documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So you want to say that my own army was wiretapping me in addition to all the other devils that were wiretapping my conversations?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: I would like to say that this conversation seized or these tapes with conversations seized at the Ratko Mladic house we believe that were -- was recorded by the security branch of Army of Republika Srpska, including you in conversation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Tell me, do you have some knowledge of the Serbian language? I assume that you do.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: I can communicate in Serbian language. I can understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could I ask you to have a look at the footnotes in the Serbian version. Who wrote the footnotes? I'll read out the first one. Number 5 says: It's possible that Svetlana (on the basis of the tone of her voice), it's possible that Svetlana is speaking. "On the basis of the tone of her voice" in brackets. And number 6, an unidentified Speaker B: It's possible that it's Karadzic, given the tone of his voice, the sound of his voice, and his interlocutor called him "President." Who wrote these footnotes?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: The transcripts were done by the members of OTP here, by the interpreters who reviewed the tapes itself, who made the transcripts, and they made -- they put also some comments here in these transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Have a look at the English version, please, the penultimate line. "Tell me, will it continue tomorrow?" Does this sound like an order to you or like a question?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: Yeah, it looks, for me, that this is a question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we see the next page in the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Does the English version also have these footnotes?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: I don't see here, at least not this version, but I believe we have the version also English one with these footnotes. But I'm not -- pretty sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you tell us why we have an unidentified Speaker A and an unidentified Speaker B in the Serbian version, whereas in the English version their identities are known, and we have the initials RK and MZ? So how can an unidentified speaker suddenly be identified as RK?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: As I said, Your Honour, because we had quite big amount of the tapes, the conversation recorded on the tapes. The tapes were reviewed by our -- our people, and if one people were -- one man was -- or woman interpreter was familiar with the voice of, for example, General Zivanovic or Mr. Karadzic, they could recognise the voices. If not, they could put some comments. And later on, probably another person will review this again and again and another review this again. Whether they have any indication who -- who is talking on the tape, they could put the correct name.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: Dr. Karadzic, how long do you think you'll -- you'll need now?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Two or three minutes, Your Excellency. Perhaps even less.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So, Mr. Blaszczyk, can we expect a literal translation of this transcript to be admitted into evidence, a translation that includes these footnotes?

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Objection. I don't know how he could answer that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: Yes. That seems to be a difficult one for this witness, Dr. Karadzic. If you want such a thing, a request in writing to the Office of the Prosecutor might be more productive.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I would do that, but the witness said that he believes that there are literal translations, so I thought it was up to him to hand them over to the Prosecution, but very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: My last question, Mr. Blaszczyk: If you could now repeat these actions that were undertaken, is there anything you would do differently? And, if so, what? And that concerns the Serbian authorities and the contact -- or, rather, interaction that the Prosecution had with the Serbian authorities.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: I am not sure whether I understood -- fully understood your question. Could you rephrase your question, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Was there anything you were unhappy about, anything you would have done differently, anything you were unhappy about with regard to the attitude the Serbian authorities had towards those searches and with regard to the entire exchange you were involved in?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: I believe, and this is my opinion, that the Serbian authorities' co-operation with these two searches with ICTY was excellent, was very good. In regards with these two searches.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Blaszczyk. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Which -- just a moment, Your Honour, it would just take me a second.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Sir, you were asked about these identified people - you'll see on the left-hand side of the screen you have the B/C/S A and B - where we see that, it starts at two minutes and goes to 2.41, is that the same conversation of the transcript in English on the right? Or is that an earlier conversation?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: This is earlier conversation I see here.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Okay. So we're not talking about -- it's not -- it's ...

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I -- just right now I noticed that this is conversation when -- starting at two minutes. This is the conversation recorded of the same tape, but this is different conversation. Also, unknown person are talking about it, and this -- yeah, and the English translation is also related to the conversation of General Zivanovic with Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: And did you have an opportunity to listen to this conversation yourself?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Did you recognise any of the voices?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: Yes, I did. I recognised the voice of Mr. Karadzic and also I am quite familiar with the voice of General Zivanovic. I recognised General Zivanovic's voice. I met him several times.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There's just one matter I would like to clarify, with your leave.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Blaskic, at the beginning of the conversation, at 2.42, Speaker B is said to be unidentified, but in brackets it says "Karadzic." Is that the case? And then there's a footnote that relates to that part.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct, but I tried to explain that a few people are not very familiar with your voice, for example, and this tape was reviewed by many of our interpreters also coming from this region, from Republika Srpska, and by investigations who are familiar with the voices also, and this is why we came to the conclusion that this is Mr. Karadzic's voice and I am sure that this is also General Zivanovic voice. Having met him several times. Also I talked to him on the phone.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. It seems that there were very few people who didn't intercept my conversations. Everyone was listening to my conversations. Thank you, Mr. Blaszczyk.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: Thank you very much for your evidence. That concludes your participation today, and have a safe journey home.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, any other matters that we can usefully deal with?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I don't believe so at this moment, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: So be it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: In that case, we'll rise for today, and we will sit again tomorrow at 9.00 a.m. Thank you. Oh, I meant to say thank you for the indulgence of the staff yesterday, and thank you very much for the technical support and indulgence for today, bearing in mind the early start. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 12th day of April, 2012, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 11.59 a.m.,
